title: Amid a tumultuous season, Jarren Duran is starting to take off at perfect time for Red Sox
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Jarren Duran's performance improves as he goes 2-for-3 in Red Sox's 4-0 win against the White Sox.
Duran, once struggling with a .195 average, now batting .341 over his last 12 games during Boston's 25-3 streak.
Boston Red Sox maintain momentum, highlighted by Duran's display of speed and strategy on the basepaths.

title: Suspect arrested in fatal shooting of Dorchester man
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Hensly Dominique Jeanty, 32, arrested and charged with murder in Dorchester man's fatal July 15 shooting.
Victim Breidy Martinez, 29, was found with a gunshot wound near 15 York St., Dorchester, and died at the scene.
Jeanty faces charges including murder and firearm offenses; shooting investigation ongoing by Boston Police.

title: Worked killed after being pinned by tractor trailer at Mass. warehouse
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A 56-year-old man was killed at a Wareham warehouse after being pinned by a tractor trailer.
The incident occurred Wednesday morning at Chatham Village Foods; the victim was pronounced dead at 9:54 a.m.
The man's identity has not been released, and the investigation by the Plymouth County District Attorney's office is ongoing.

title: Abreu homers again, Gray gets 14th victory as Red Sox beat White Sox 4-0 for 7th straight win
author: The Associated Press
bullets: The Red Sox secured their seventh consecutive win, defeating the White Sox 4-0 with help from Wilyer Abreu's home run.
Sonny Gray achieved his 14th victory, tying for the major league lead, allowing three hits and striking out eight.
Boston's pitchers delivered the team's 11th shutout of the season, with relievers completing a four-hitter.

title: Huge basking shark spotted off South Shore beach, white sharks appear near Maine, Cape Cod
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A large basking shark was seen near Humarock Beach in Scituate on August 4, drawing attention from beachgoers.
White sharks have been spotted in New England, including near North Beach Island in Chatham and Pine Point Beach in Maine.
Increased shark sightings are attributed to peak season, conservation efforts, and more public documentation via smartphones and drones.

title: Man shot to death mid-morning on Blue Hill Avenue
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A man was shot and killed near 564 Blue Hill Ave in Dorchester around 10:15 a.m. on Wednesday.
The victim sought help in an apartment building before collapsing and being pronounced dead at a hospital.
Boston police are conducting an ongoing investigation and request any information be reported to their Homicide Unit.

title: Former MLB GM says Red Sox had ‘biggest overpay’ before trade deadline
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Red Sox's trade for Curtis Mead was labeled MLB's biggest overpay by former GM Jim Bowden.
Curtis Mead injured his wrist in his second at-bat with Boston, sidelining him for 6-8 weeks.
Red Sox traded pitcher Connelly Early to acquire Mead; Early had a 3.44 ERA over 17 starts in 2026.

title: Brockton mayor suing state, says 2025 crash involving State Trooper left him disabled
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Brockton Mayor Moises Rodrigues is suing Massachusetts, claiming a 2025 crash with a State Trooper left him partially disabled.
The accident occurred on May 11, 2025, when Trooper Augustine Moore allegedly crossed into Rodrigues' lane, causing the collision.
Rodrigues seeks a jury trial for damages, claiming medical bills exceeded $32,000 and lost wages totaled $3,554.

title: Grant Williams explains relationship dynamic between Jayson Tatum, Jaylen Brown
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Grant Williams clarifies that Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown had mutual respect and no personal issues during their time with the Celtics.
NBA insider Shams Charania stated that Tatum and Brown weren't close personally, despite their success on the court together.
Jayson Tatum expressed appreciation and respect for Jaylen Brown after Brown's trade to the Philadelphia 76ers.

title: Cyclospora cases climb to 147 in Mass., but officials say season remains within historical range
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Massachusetts reports 147 cyclospora cases from May 1 to Aug. 1, linked to contaminated iceberg lettuce from Mexico.
Despite increased cases, officials see no large outbreaks in Massachusetts; season remains within historical case range.
The FDA linked recalled Taylor Farms lettuce to food-service locations, contributing to the multi-state cyclosporiasis outbreak.
